$comment: Derived by engine/scripts/state_map.py. Do not edit — state_check compares this against the repository in both directions. There is no generation timestamp on purpose: it would change on every run and the validator would have to learn to ignore a field. Keyed on source_commit instead.

0_integrity.why: every licence file the metadata declares is present, every extra's status matches what the code imports, and no docstring names a module that does not exist

1_architecture.why: the dossier exists and regenerates in CI, so every node now carries the evidence a person needs; what is missing is the person. 0 of 507 rows have been ruled on, and no machine may raise that number

2_evidence.why: the claim registry exists and is checked in CI, and status is recomputed rather than stored — but a registry is not the gate: 6 of 16 claims are still UNKNOWN or CONTRADICTED, so 'important claims have evidence' is not yet true

3_implementation.why: the suite is green and the mutation probe kills every mutation, and the capability registry now measures coverage per capability: 8 capabilities at {'E4_INTEGRATED': 8}. What is still missing is scale — 8 is a first, deliberately small cut, not the platform's full surface, and E5-E7 are unreachable from a repository scan for every one of them
evidence: mutate.py exists and is in CI

4_integration.why: no integration evidence has been collected

5_production.why: nothing is deployed; DOCKER.md and compose.yaml exist and no workflow builds them, and a configuration is not a deployment. The app now has the pieces a deployment platform would check (liveness route: True, readiness route: True), which narrows what a first deploy still needs, not whether one exists

6_security.why: controls that ARE in the repository run on every pull request or release (dependency audit in CI: True, dependency review on PR diffs: True, Dependabot config: True, build provenance attested in the release workflow: True, an SBOM generated and read back against the package it describes in the release workflow: True, every GitHub Action pinned to a commit SHA: 20/20); what is absent is any signed PUBLISHED artifact, since no release exists — none of this has run for real. CodeQL and secret scanning are GitHub settings rather than files, so a repository scan cannot see either from the tree alone; C-015 in state/claims.jsonl carries the one live exception — attempting an advanced-setup CodeQL workflow confirmed default setup is already enabled, evidence a repository scan cannot rederive and this function does not claim

7_observability.why: omnex.obs emits traces, metrics and a cost ledger in-process; nothing is collected from a running deployment because there is none

8_evaluation.why: omnex.evals gates on newly-failing cases in the suite; no agent runs in production to evaluate

9_autonomy.why: the run ledger holds 67 hash-chained run(s) (chain intact: True) at levels ['L3', 'L3_REPOSITORY', 'L4_EXTERNAL'], so actions taken here are bounded and auditable — what this gate asks for and still has no evidence of is an autonomous run against a deployment: 3 run(s) are recorded above L3 and 1 of those recorded a successful outcome

10_distribution.why: the release path is in the repository and in the gate block (release_check.py: True, release.yml: True); whether an artifact was actually published is not a fact about this tree, and C-005, C-011 and C-013 in state/claims.jsonl are where that is tracked

11_commercial.why: no external user has obtained the software; 0 listings live

12_economic.why: no revenue log exists — 0 recorded is not 0 earned, and BUSINESS.md refuses to render it as a measurement
